grid.coordinates: lon = x0 + (col + 0.5) * dx, lat = y0 + (row + 0.5) * dy with dy NEGATIVE; x0/y0 are the grid's WEST and NORTH edges, and the source's `lat`/`lon` are the pixel CENTRES those edges imply
grid.extent_note: [west, south, east, north] in degrees; ALL surfaces — land, ice, inland and coastal water and the open ocean — no land mask
grid.no_tile_corners: a plain geographic grid: the affine rule above IS the lat/lon of every pixel and every tile corner, so no corner table is stored
grid.row_order: row 0 is the NORTHERNMOST row (the source netCDF's DESCENDING `lat` axis, 89.97917 .. -89.97917, checked on the real 2025-07-01 files); col 0 is the westernmost, lon -179.97917
grid.same_grid_as: pace4k and oc4k — the ocean-colour stores share this grid exactly, so one tile scheme reads all three
grid.source_variables: rhos (float32 [lat, lon, wavelength], _FillValue -32767, dimensionless) of PACE_OCI_L3M_SFREFL v3.1, eight bands of its 122, on this grid with no resampling

nrt_boundary.policy: final files only: NRT days past the final edge are after_record, NRT-only days inside it are absent_upstream

qc_policy: FINAL (refined) files only; NRT files are never stored — a day past the final edge is `after_record` (counted `nrt_after_final` where an NRT file exists) and a day inside the record with only an NRT file is `absent_upstream` (counted `nrt_only_inside_record`). The producer masked ATMFAIL, CLDICE, HIGLINT, HILT, HISATZEN and HISOLZEN at binning and no per-pixel flag reaches level 3; the store applies nothing further. The fill (-32767) and any non-finite value become NaN; a value outside -0.05..1.5 (the producer's own valid range) becomes NaN and is counted (`out_of_bounds`), never clipped. ALL SURFACES are kept — no land mask. `rhos` is corrected for Rayleigh scattering and gases, NOT for aerosol. Every frame passes two checks (E-092 §6): an independent single-pixel re-read equal to the frame to float16 precision (refused otherwise), and the dark-water test on rhos_2258 over the BGC product's clear-water pixels (soft failures kept and named, a gross failure refused)
